label: Plenitude does not fix the residual observational probability
summary: Analyst mathematics, attribution deferred. Draft authored in PR #2143 (author model unrecorded); repaired, registered and verified here. Question: does an infinite population of universes fix the probability of a residual observation? Verified answer for the encoded models: no. (1) On one roster Bool x Nat with each type repeated infinitely, Bernoulli(p) x geometric(1/2) product measures give every interior p positive point mass and true-fiber mass p, so the fixed roster, type map and supplied possibility profiles do not identify that mass. (2) Nested exhaustive finite cutoffs give every positive rational relative frequency a/(a+b). (3) Positive reweighting of the two observer cells of an existing sampling row reaches every interior rational likelihood when the other-observer cell has positive mass; with that cell absent the construction fails, preserving the #1381 screening-off boundary. (4) Transporting (1) along a fiber-preserving bijection gives the shared lemma: on every countable carrier with an infinite event and infinite complement each interior event probability has a point-positive normalized measure. This is the single copy of the interior-mass lemma; #2142 reuses it. Limits: these are non-identification results for bare carriers, cutoffs and weights. They do not show that no probability is warranted: a physically warranted generator, measure or observer rule can still fix a prediction, as the reviewed #1569 causal-entropic comparison does under its assumptions. The corollaries no_scope_decoder (total_factor_iff form of the third conjunct of (1)) and threshold_not_evidence_only (the #736 EvidenceOnly criterion applied to the probability-at-least-one-half proposition) are proved in the Solution but not registered, since both follow directly from the scope data being constant across the compared measures. Next test: whether competing physically warranted measures and record proxies agree on residual bins beyond observer viability, and whether an independently justified design likelihood bounds the same probabilities (#1734).
